points: A storage engine decides how a database lays rows out on disk, and B-trees and LSM-trees move cost between reads, writes and space.
Meta found InnoDB wasted 25% to 30% of each block, and its LSM-tree engine made instances 62.3% smaller for the same data.
Discord's Cassandra nodes fell behind on compaction and tombstones, and moving to ScyllaDB cut 177 nodes to 72.
An LSM-tree buffers writes in memory, flushes sorted files and merges them later, trading cheap writes for extra read checks and background work.
